App.DebugView.engineLogFooter: The engine's last 400 lines, the newest last (37 so far); once there are 400, the oldest go as new ones come, so the lines move up while you read - Copy keeps them as they are. Each line starts with a time in seconds on the Mac's clock: the gaps between lines are what count. Console shows them too, as they happen: choose this Mac, turn on Action > Include Info Messages, press Start, then search for subsystem:net.lizardlounge.deadwax.
App.DebugView.testSoundsFooter: Songs 1 to 8 are three beeps each: click one to play the album from it and count the beeps - all three, every time? Songs 9 and 10 are one tone cut in two: played one into the other, the tone should never break. A song downloaded to this Mac plays from there, as every song does; "Stream even when downloaded" (under Downloads) streams it instead, to hear the two side by side. The record's engine beside the song plays a run of its own - a chord taken from 1 s, scratched back and forth and let go, again and again - over whatever plays here. Start it while a test sound plays: you should hear both, the test sound unchanged, and stopping or starting it should never be heard in the test sound. Its Clock should hold within a millisecond or two once settled.
